 and compare outputs before trusting a seeded label; an unobservable mutation
 measures nothing.
+
+### Comparing two runs
+
+    px1 eval-compare --cases cases.json --before old/results.json --after new/results.json
+
+Use it after changing a prompt, a tool or a model: run `eval-run` before and
+after with the same cases, then compare. Each labelled bug is tested with
+Fisher's exact test on found versus missed runs, and the pooled result is
+reported too. A difference counts only at p ≤ 0.10. That is loose on purpose: with
+three runs a side the smallest possible p-value is 0.10 (3 of 3 against 0 of 3), so
+a stricter bar would call everything noise. Two found against none, or one extra
+find, is shown as "same". The report warns when the after run flags more on clean
+changes, since more findings can mean more false alarms. Pooling treats runs of
+different bugs as independent, which they are not entirely: read the overall
+verdict as a guide, and prefer more runs over a cleverer statistic.

explanations.title: Compare two evaluation runs
explanations.summary: Adds `px1 eval-compare` to score two result files against the same repeat dataset. It supports configurable finding matching, can save the Markdown report, and also prints it to stdout; input and scoring errors stop the command.

explanations.title: Distinguish changes from run noise
explanations.summary: Compares each labelled bug’s found/missed counts with a two-sided Fisher exact test and calls a change better or worse only when p ≤ 0.10. It also calculates a pooled verdict and omits labels with no scored runs; reports for different case or label counts are rejected.

explanations.title: Report quality and false-alarm changes
explanations.summary: The report summarizes recall, precision, clean-run noise, unstable bugs, and cost for both runs, then shows per-bug counts and verdicts. It warns when clean-run noise rises, since additional findings may be false alarms.

explanations.title: Expose the comparison command
explanations.summary: Recognizes `eval-compare` as a CLI command and includes it in the usage list, making the comparison workflow available through the main executable.
